transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-15 14:30 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood Product), Sanjay (Aurora CTO), Marta (Head of ML), Devon (Platform Eng), Leah (Security)

Auto Summary: demo of Model Catalog; show filters for open models, run through benchmarks for latency/quality, review compatibility matrix (quantization, kernels, hardware targets), discuss Dedicated vs Hosted for PHI; next steps pilot.

[00:00] Maya: all right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining im maya from Redwood Inference, im the account lead for aurora, with me today diego our solutions engineer and lina from product. hows everyone doing?
[00:08] Sanjay: good, thanks maya. we've been looking forward to seeing the catalog — want to see what open models we can use with PHI, and what the perf looks like.
[00:14] Marta: yeah, specifically clinical summarization and templated notes, low latency for internal tools is important.
[00:20] Maya: perfect, that's exactly what we'll walk thru. quick agenda: catalog filters, benchmark pages, compatibility matrix, deployment options, then q&a and next steps.
[00:30] Diego: jumping in, this is the model catalog home screen — you can filter by license (open / commercial), task (summarization, chat, embeddings), tokenization, and compute profile. i should note our model names sometimes map to community names, there can be subtle mismatches in the transcription, so we'll flag the canonical model id in the table.
[01:02] [screen share noise]
[01:15] Diego: ok here's a demo filter: open models -> summarization -> <= 512 context. results: Llama-3-13B (community build), Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-7b-instruct, and a couple quantized variants. note the "compatibility" column shows supported runtimes (TRT, AOT, PTX) and quant formats (8-bit, 4-bit, q8_4). we also show verified throughput for a 1k token prompt on A100 and T4, but there is a note that bench numbers vary by sequence length.
[01:50] Marta: quick question — how do you measure quality across models? are you using rouge/bleu or human evals?
[01:56] Lina: good q. our default bench harness runs a mix: perplexity baselines, task-specific ROUGE for summarization, and a small human-annotated pass against a medical prompt set (anonymized). we surface a quality score and delta vs our reference model. we also surface hallucination flags from our evals.
[02:18] Sanjay: is that medical set public? we need to know domain match.
[02:22] Lina: not public, but we can share metrics and the prompt sets we used, and for your pilot we can re-run with your sample prompts.
[02:31] [02:31] Devon: about compatibility — we run on a mix of GCP A2/GPU and some on-prem servers with A100s. do you support mixed hardware routing and autoscaling?
[02:40] Diego: yes, smart routing can route by region or by capacity tier; for mixed hardware we recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput — you can pin model variants to specific pools. autoscaling policies can scale by qps or queue length and we support burst capacity into hosted if needed.
[02:58] Leah: on the security side, PHI residency and KMS are critical. what options for encryption and audit logs?
[03:06] Maya: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), audit logs with per-request metadata, and Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) where control plane is customer-managed. we'll attach the SOC2 summary and our KMS integration guide.
[03:20] Marta: great. about quantization: some models seem to lose accuracy when 4-bit quantized. do you have recommendations?
[03:27] Diego: yes, we include quantization profiles in the compatibility matrix. for example Llama-3-13B q4f16 performs well on summarization with minimal delta vs fp16 for many prompts; some 7B models actually see bigger regression when aggressively quantized. we recommend running a short RTT eval on your prompts — that helps pick the right model+quant profile.
[03:50] [03:50] Maya: i'm opening the compatibility matrix spreadsheet — columns: model_id, license, recommended_quant_profiles, supported_kernels, recommended_hardware, verified_latency@seq128@A100, verified_latency@seq128@T4, notes. link: https://app.redwood.ai/catalog/compatibility?sheet=aurora-sample (note: demo link)
[04:12] Sanjay: can you explain the kernel column — what are the kernel options?
[04:16] Diego: sure — kernels are the optimized execution paths: fused-attention kernels for A100, triton kernels for RTX, and a fallback cpu path. some models also have AOT compiled variants for lower latency at cost of larger binaries. the matrix shows what we've validated. sometimes the kernel name in the community repo is slightly different which can cause mapping issues, we try to reconcile names in the canonical id field.
[04:43] Marta: do you support continuous batching and prefix caching? we need low p95 for UI use.
[04:49] Diego: yes, our runtime does continuous batching with latency-aware batching windows and KV prefix caching. we also have per-route config to tune batch window vs p95. for p95-sensitive UI we typically set a smaller batching window and enable cache warmups.
[05:07] Leah: any compliance limitations for Private on-prem? like auditability and integrations?
[05:12] Maya: Private includes full audit logging, SAML/SSO integrations, and can be configured to ship audit logs to your SIEM. the on-prem package includes a support plan for upgrades and security patches.
[05:25] [05:25] Sanjay: pricing — open models are cheaper but do you still charge for tokens and instance hours?
[05:30] Maya: yes pricing is usage-based for hosted (per-token + throughput). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits; we provide cost models in the spreadsheet. open model choice impacts per-token cost mainly via latency and compute footprint. we'll send a cost comparison in the matrix.
[05:45] Devon: for the pilot where we run say 2000 requests/day, what is the recommended setup?
[05:50] Diego: for that volume and low-latency needs, a small dedicated pool on A100 with 2-3 GPUs and a fallback to hosted for burst is typical; or if you can't commit, start hosted trial with autoscale and then convert to Dedicated once you see stable qps.
[06:07] Marta: can we see a live run of Llama-3-13B vs Mistral-Instruct on a sample clinical prompt?
[06:12] Diego: yes i'll run two side-by-side with same prompt. note as a demo these are on a trimmed sequence length to keep latency reasonable.
[06:25] [06:25] Diego: prompt: "Summarize patient encounter: 56yo female with htn, cxr negative, started lisinopril, follow-up in 2 weeks. create short SOAP note."
[06:40] [06:40] Llama-3-13B (demo): "S: 56F with history of hypertension presented for routine follow-up. O: chest x-ray unremarkable, vitals stable. A: hypertension, medication initiation of lisinopril. P: start lisinopril 10 mg daily; follow-up in 2 weeks; counsel on lifestyle."
[07:02] [07:02] Mistral-Instruct-7B (demo): "Chief complaint: routine follow-up for HTN. Exam: cxr negative, no acute findings. Impression: new lisinopril started. Plan: continue medication, return in two weeks, monitor bp. consider labs if symptoms."
[07:30] Marta: both look reasonable; any hallucination scoring?
[07:33] Lina: we flagged mentions that require verification (e.g., misattributed lab results) — in this prompt none popped up. we'll surface hallucination score for each result in the bench.
[07:44] Sanjay: what's the expected latency difference?
[07:47] Diego: in our verified numbers at seq128 Llama-3-13B on A100 was ~220ms median and 450ms p95; Mistral-7B was ~140ms median and 280ms p95. on T4 these numbers shift up. we'll share exact table.
[08:05] Leah: can we enforce no data retention for clinical inputs on hosted?
[08:09] Maya: yes you can opt out of retention on hosted, but for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private; hosted no-retain is available but you still need to evaluate legal posture. we'll share the retention SLA.
[08:25] [08:25] Devon: how do you handle model rollouts/rollbacks in production if perf regressions appear?
[08:31] Diego: rollouts are built into the Console: canary percentages, A/B, automatic fallback policies to previous model or to a cheaper variant. we also integrate eval hooks to detect regressions on a set of golden prompts and trigger alerts.
[08:48] Sanjay: about the compatibility matrix, can you include kernel binaries sizes? some ops team members worry about disk footprint for AOT compiled models.
[08:56] Maya: yes we can add binary size and load time as additional columns. we'll include that in the spreadsheet we send.
[09:05] Marta: last thing — do you have any recommended open models that are specifically tuned for medical text?
[09:11] Lina: open models specifically tuned for clinical are rare; we often recommend using an instruction-tuned open model and adding a domain-adaptive finetune or retrieval augmentation. we also have a few model variants in the catalog that were finetuned on public biomedical corpora; we'll flag those in the matrix.
[09:30] [09:30] Maya: ok quick recap and next steps: we'll share the compatibility matrix, benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2 summary and KMS guide; diego will prepare the pilot runbook and a 2-hour kickoff to get credentials and infra; marta will share prompt sets and sample notes. agreed?
[09:48] Sanjay: yes, sounds good.
[09:50] Marta: yep.
[09:52] Leah: please include the SAML integration doc for our IdP.
[09:55] Maya: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email and add calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[10:00] End of call

Notes: occasional transcription mislabels (speaker IDs) and auto captions errors present, canonical links and docs to be sent post-call.
